characters.name: open/close all folders
characters.description: The Ghost with the Most. A shady "bio-exorcist", Betelgeuse (pronounced "Beetlejuice") is a ghost that professionally scares the living out of other ghosts' haunts, and loves his work. He's very easy to summon — saying his name three times is all that's needed — but very difficult to get rid of once he's there, because he's steadfastly determined to remain in the world of the living as long as he can manage. Abhorrent Admirer: By the sequel he appears to have genuinely fallen for Lydia, calling her "the love of my life" when they're face-to-face for the first time in decades. Lydia still finds him creepy and disgusting and repeatedly tells him to leave her alone. Abnormal Limb Rotation Range: Betelgeuse's head spins freely, apparently not within his complete control.noteIn the original script, Betelgeuse died by suicide via hanging. Given how ghosts either reflect or maintain attributes from their death, this may be from cracked or outright destroyed neck vertebrae. AcCENT upon the Wrong SylLABle: Adam Maitland continually mispronounces his name different ways: "Beetle-geiss", "Beetle-meier" or even "This beetle guy". Affably Evil: Zig-zags between this andFaux Affably Evil. While Betelgeuse is not a friend to anyone and is unsafe for women, he's just so damncharming. He offers to make Barbara and Adam an Italian dinner, attempts their requested task (though not to their liking), and feels genuinely offended when they interfere. He is initially baffled by Lydia's desire to be dead but offers to help since she insists. Despite his quirky traits, Betelgeuse is ultimately a crude, perverted troublemaker without restraint or self-control, making him dangerous to be around for long. His enjoyment may stem from a childish desire to torment and nearly kill with his pranks. He is shown to be reckless and harmful, evidenced by his nearly killing Lydia's father as a snake, attacking Maxie Dean and his spouse, and using Lydia to gain permanent access to the living world.

characters.name: Adam Maitland
characters.description: A humble countryman who runs a hardware store and enjoys building miniature models. AcCENT upon the Wrong SylLABle: When Adam finds the advert for Betelgeuse, he actually says the name three times, but because he pronounces it "Bay-til Guy-ce", the incantation doesn't work. Body Horror: Having his head cut off, then stretching his nose out while shoving his hand into the back of his head and growing eyes on his fingers. Establishing Character Moment: Adam and the spider. Instead of squashing it, he only comments on its size and lets it go free, showing him to be anice guy. Fanboy: He's shown to be one ofHarry Belafonte, as he enjoys listening to his music while working on the model. As a ghost, he tries to frighten everyone (save for Lydia) away by possessing everyone into doing a dance number to "Day-O (The Banana Boat Song),” and at the end of the film, he rewards Lydia for getting an A on her math test by using his powers to play "Jump in the Line" while Lydia dances in the air.

characters.name: Barbara Maitland
characters.description: A homemaker who was planning on starting a family before her death. Action Girl: A downplayed example, since she doesn't have too many action scenes, but the scenes where she deals with the sandworm definitely put her here. Big Damn Heroes:Just as Betelgeuse is about to marry Lydia, Barbara comes in riding on a Sandworm that eats Betelgeuse, stopping the wedding in the nick of time. Body Horror: Ripping her face off, then stretching out her jaws and setting her eyes in her open mouth. Did You Just Punch Out Cthulhu?: Barbara wangs the Sand Worm right on the nose, causing it to retreat... and then later befriends it!

characters.name: Lydia Deetz
characters.description: A goth girl who can see ghosts. Lydia has a strained relationship with her father and stepmother, neither of whom she feels pays any degree of attention to her, and latches onto the Maitlands as her first genuine friends. In the sequel, some thirty-odd years after the first movie, she has become a medium and paranormal investigator with a fairly successful TV show, alongside a failing relationship with her own (very skeptical) daughter. Abhorrent Admirer: Gains one in the form of Betelgeuse, who, while at first was only interested in marrying her to gain access to the living world, seems to have genuinely fallen for her in the sequel. However, because he has traumatized her as a teenager with his antics and retains hisDirty Old Manstatus, Lydia is as repulsed by him now as she was back then, if not more so. The only reason she agrees to any interaction with him now is only because it's the only option she has. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Played for drama. Her show is a source of embarrassment for Astrid, who faces mockery from her fellow students. Amicable Exes: In the sequel, Lydia tells Astrid that her relationship with her husband and Astrid's father, Richard, was over long before his death.But when they meet again in the Afterlife, there's nothing but affection between Lydia and Richard, and they're both very proud of Astrid. Broken Bird: The sequel shows that life and loss through the following three decades have reduced her from aPerky Gothinto this. She eventually regains much of her old spirit, and ironically it's mostly due to dealing with Betelgeuse all over again.Now... if only she could be certain that Betelgeuse is really forever out of her life... again.

characters.name: Delia Deetz
characters.description: An eccentric contemporary artist and Lydia's stepmother. Actually Pretty Funny: Admits she finds the tumultuous mother-daughter relationship between Astrid and Lydia humorous because she thinks it’s karma for how Lydia treated Delia when she was a teenager. Alliterative Name:DeliaDeetz. Arbitrary Skepticism: Subverted. She at first refuses to believe Lydia about her claims about the house being haunted, but comes to believe it immediately after the dinner scene. Her agent Bernard, on the other hand, refuses to believe it happened, even though he was there. It is also an avenue to attract Maxie Dean, an art patron she desperately wants to ingratiate since he and his wife are huge believers in the paranormal. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other:After dying in the sequel, she promises to find Charles and haunt Lydia and Astrid till they live long and happy lives as a family, with Lydia and Astrid looking happy at that.It's also that the one room that Charles asked Delia not to alter in any way remained the same in the sequel, revealing she did honor his request even after Charles died.

characters.name: Charles Deetz
characters.description: A city native that just wants to retreat to the country. And I Must Scream: After being killed in a shark attack, Charles is damned to wander the afterlife with most of his upper body missing. He can still clearly see, hear, and speak though, so how much this actually affects him is unclear. Body Horror: Due to the way the afterlife works,he ends up manifesting not just headless, but also havinga large curved arc of his torso missing.To put the cherry on top, any time he speaks its through what remains of his esophagus, which sputters blood at whoever he's talking to. Bumbling Dad: He's not the most hands-on parent, but he's shown calling Lydia "pumpkin" and demonstrating genuine affection toward her. Everyone Has Standards: He's excited about profiting off his new haunted house, and resorts to a séance/exorcism to force Adam and Barbara to go along with it. However he's unaware that doing so will cause the Maitlands to suffer aFate Worse than Death, and tries unsuccessfully to get Otho to stop the ritual when it becomes apparent that it is harming them.

characters.name: Astrid Deetz
characters.description: Lydia's daughter. Astrid is a firm skeptic with little interest in the supernatural, and is on very poor terms with her mother, whom she views as a fraud and a profound source of social embarassment. All of the Other Reindeer: Her introductory scene shows her being mocked by aGirl Possefor her mom’s TV show. Babies Ever After: Subverted as the endinghas her giving birth to Betelgeuse's inner child, then Lydia wakes up from the nightmare. Brainy Brunette: Her hair is as black as Lydia's, andafter only a quick glance at the Handbook for the Recently Deceased, she's able to find a loophole to invalidate her mother's deal with Betelgeuse, saving Lydia once again from being forced to marry him. Daddy's Girl: She was much closer to her late father, Richard, than she is to her mother. Lydia (who can see other ghosts just fine) being unable to see Astrid's father's spirit only drives them further apart.

characters.name: Juno
characters.description: The demonic Director of the Neitherworld Bureau of Customs and Processing. Adaptational Villainy: In the stage musical,Juno is changed into Beetlejuice's alcoholic and overbearing, abusive mother. It's suggested thather bad parenting might be a reason Beetlejuice turned out the way he did. While the movie-version of Juno disliked the living,she was content with letting the Deetzes and the Maitlands coexist; musical-Juno, on the other hand, tries to keep Lydia in the Neitherworld after she enters in an attempt to escape Beetlejuice and locate her mother. Adaptation Name Change: In the DC tryout, her name was changed to Mrs. Eileen Shoggoth, or simply Mrs. Shoggoth. After Miss Argentina was added on Broadway, her name was changed back to Juno. Abusive Parents:Throughout the play, Beetlejuice mentions his terrible mother, who is later revealed to be her, and she goes as far as to say she wishes he had never been born and she had left like his father. She is the reason for his crazy powers and is strong enough to throw BJ around like a ragdoll. The Alcoholic: According to Beetlejuice, Junoloved booze more than him, and spent most of his childhood drunk.

characters.name: Miss Argentina
characters.description: A former troubled Beauty Queen and an assistant to Juno. Adaptational Nice Guy: While the movie had her be snarky around the Maitlands, the musical has hertake pity on Lydia and try to convince her to return to Earth and live her life while she still can.Her song manages to get through to her and it's one of the reasons Lydia stops her suicidal ideation. Afterlife Angst: Her music number, "What I Know Now," is all about how miserable the afterlife is and how she regrets not living life to the fullest while she still could. Ascended Extra: She has little impact on the movie, beyond being a receptionist with little patience towards the Maitlands, explaining they must remain in their house until their paperwork is finished being processed in 125 years. In the musical, while she only appears in one scene, she gets her own song which builds upon her backstory as a depressed beauty queen who wasDriven to Suicide, using it to encourage Lydia that death doesn't solve her problems and to live her life while she still can. Driven to Suicide: While she still had her little accident, the musical goes on to explain she was a beauty queen and a party girl who had low self-esteem and depression and took her own life in order to end her suffering, something she regrets.

characters.name: Delores
characters.description: Beetlejuice's ex-wife who has unfinished business with him. Ascended Extra: Her severed finger appears in the first movie when Beetlejuice pulls it out to retrieve a wedding ring. He claims she meant nothing to him. But in the sequel, you can understand what he really meant by that. Asshole Victim:After eating the souls of three genuinely innocent bystanders in the realm of the dead, everyone is against her; even Wolf Jackson, in spite of his beef with Beetlejuice and later attempting to arrest him, sympathetically warns him to be on the lookout for her. When she actually encounters the rest of the cast during the climax, the Deetzes actually help Betelgeuse get rid of her by blindsiding her with a hungry Sandworm. Big Bad: Though she is not always onscreen and doesn't meet much of the heroes, Delores' hunt for Beetlejuice drives the plot of the sequel forward and she's the greatest threat to everyone's lives, looming over the desperate actions of Beetlejuice to escape her once and for all at all moments. Big Bad Wannabe: She, along with Jeremy, is set up as the true main bad guy of the movie, whose actions force the heroes and Beetlejuice to form a temporary alliance. However, while she lasts longer than Jeremy, both are ultimately disposed of before the true climax, when Beetlejuice reclaims his position as trueBig Badand final obstacle for Lydia and Astrid.

characters.name: Wolf Jackson
characters.description: A former actor turned ghost detective tracking down Beetlejuice and Delores. Actor Allusion: Willem Dafoe originally played a detective inAmerican Psycho, a film that also included Justin Theroux andan actorfamously known for playing Batman. Body Horror: The side of his head is missing a large amount of flesh, exposing his skull and brain which have since discolored. Catchphrase: Wolf has an obsession with "keepin' it real", which extends to having his secretary keep him from forgetting he wasn't actually a cop when he was alive. Closest Thing We Got: In life, he was an actor famous for playing a hotshot police detective. In the Netherworld, he's been placed in charge of the police department because he's effectively the only ghost they have on hand that's remotely qualified for the job. He keeps having to be reminded that he is not technically a real cop.

characters.name: Bob
characters.description: A shrunken head ghost who works for Betelgeuse, and his second-in-command. Actually a Doombot:Played for Laughs. When Betelgeuse orders Bob to take charge, Bob dresses up like him. When Betelgeuse sees this, he considers Bob to be a good decoy to keep Delores distracted. Character Celebrity Endorsement:He has his own Google commercial. Deader than Dead:He gets his soul consumed by Delores, resulting in him completely ceasing to exist even in the Afterlife. Eye Scream:After he’s turned into an empty, rubbery husk, both of his eyeballs pop like balloons.

characters.name: Otho
characters.description: Delia's frequently mentioned Guru. Adaptational Sexuality: While his film counterpart was implied to be gay, a scrapped song from the musical, "I am Very Good at Running Cults," had him brag about having slept with (and murdered) a lot of women. Though the canonicity of this is debatable. Adaptational Villainy: While the film had Otho be an arrogantKnow-Nothing Know-It-Allwho was a genuinely polite family friend to the Deetzes andregretted what his actions did to the Maitlands, the stage musical changes himinto a charlatan who took advantage of Delia's depression. He confesses after Beetlejuice decides to kill him that his real name is Kevin and he's from Nutley, New Jersey. Adaptation Name Change: He confessesbefore Beetlejuice tortures him that his real name is Kevin. Broken Pedestal: To his "disciple" Delia, after he spells it out he's a fraud, so she wastes no time in letting Beetlejuice torture him.

characters.name: Maxie and Sarah Dean
characters.description: A wealthy real estate couple and the heads of Botco Industries, whom the Deetzes turn to. Actually Pretty Funny: The annoyinglystoicMaxie cannot help himself but giggle whenLydiapoints out that Otho can't even change a tire. Asshole Victim: Both of them are possibly killed by Betelgeuse, but it's hard to feel sorry for them after they spend the entire dinner acting like aloof, callous jerks. The Bore: The movie implies both of them are dead inside. The only time they display any actual emotion is when Lydia unleashes Betelgeuse and he begins to wreak havoc. Even Evil Has Standards: Averted. They are present at the seance and are the only ones who don't seem to care the Maitlands are outright rotting in front of them, even after Lydia protests that they're clearly in pain.

characters.name: Jane & "Little Jane" Butterfield
characters.description: Both realtors, and Barbara's relatives. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Jane may talk sweet, but she only cares about trying to sell the Maitlands' house without their consent. Establishing Character Moment: Jane is introduced driving up to the Maitlands's house despite knowing that they are trying to have a staycation and wish to be left alone, so she can try to convince them to hold a showing for their house to a prospective buyer despite the fact that she isn't the Maitlands's realtor, the house isn't on the market, and they have apparently told her that they have no interest in selling the houserepeatedly. Innocently Insensitive: When trying to talk Barbara into selling their house, Jane offhandedly mentions that the house is meant for a family. Barbara, who's implied to want a child but seems to be infertile, is visibly hurt by the statement. It may not be so innocent as she doesn't even hesitate to sell their house right after they died, and the extended ending confirms she's trying to do the same thing with the Deetzes. Jerkass: Selling her cousin's house after she and her husband just died cements Jane as this. She also let the new owners have all of the Maitlands' stuff, including their photos and wedding clothing. She may not have had any way of knowing about the whole afterlife situation, but it's still flagrantly disrespectful.

characters.name: Rory
characters.description: Lydia's latest fiancé and the producer of her showGhost House. Asshole Victim:Gets eaten by a Sand Worm alongside Delores, normally a horrific fate none would wish on anyone, but considering the reveal of his nature as a despicableGold Diggerand his sleazy attitude, no one sheds a tear for him, especially Lydia and Astrid. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Acts like a charming, down-to-Earth,Understanding Boyfriendto Lydia, but it soon becomes blatantly obvious to the audience (as well as Astrid and Delia) that he's a selfish and manipulative man who doesn't actually care about Lydia's problems.In truth, he's nothing but a sleazy gold-digger who is happy to take advantage of Lydia and is only planning to marry her for the money he'd make as her husband. Crocodile Tears:When he proposes to Lydia and she turns him down, he fakes crying and acts heartbroken to get her to change her mind. Devil in Plain Sight: It's pretty obvious early on that he's a smarmyJerkasswho's only interested in getting into Lydia's good graces while not actually caring about her problems.Him admitting to being aGold Diggerwhile under the influence ofTruth Serumonly reveals that his feelings for Lydia were not even skin-deep.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: General tropes about Adam and Barbara Maitland. Afterlife Angst: Initially averted until the Deetz family buys their home. Ascended to a Higher Plane of Existence: Their absence in the sequel is established by Lydia as them finding a loophole, allowing them to leave the house and move on. Bedsheet Ghost: While trying to scare the Deetz family. It didn't work: Charles thinks one of them was Lydia trying to play a prank, Delia is too doped out on "Prince Valium" to notice them, and Lydia thinks (at first) that it's Charles and Delia playing some kinky bedroom game. Lampshaded by Barbara. Beware the Nice Ones: They're very nice and friendly people (so nice, in fact, they're terrible at haunting the living), but should you do anything to threaten Lydia, they will stop at nothing to protect her, even if it means killing you. Just ask Betelgeuse.

characters.name: Beetlejuice
characters.description: The Ghost With the Most again, although this incarnation is much more weird and gross rather than cruel and lecherous. Adaptational Dye-Job: His film and theatre counterparts have green hair, while this incarnation has blond hair. Adaptational Heroism: Big time. He may still be a jerk and a sneaky scammer like he was in the film, but here he's given more heroic traits to balance his flaws. In particular, he cares genuinely about Lydia and does his best for her happiness without any strings attached, unlike his film counterpart. Adaptational Name Change: In the movie, his name was actually spelled "Betelgeuse". Here, it's spelled as it sounds and as written in the title. Adaptational Nice Guy:He's a much more benevolent (though still crooked) figure in the animated series than he was in the movie. Rather than wanting to actually cause physical harm to people, he's content with merely driving them crazy - he even has a license to do so.Also, since this series had to be toned down from the original film for children's television, his perverted tendencies had to be excised from his character. He does nothing worse than the occasional approving gaze at attractive adult female ghosts.

characters.name: JacquesLaLean
characters.description: Beyond the Impossible: How can askeletonbe overweight? Dem Bones: He's a living skeleton. Easily Scattered Skeleton: He frequently falls apart, usually due to Beetlejuice's pranks.The show milks it for all it's worth. French Jerk: Inverted. Jacques is a perfect gentleman, particularly to Mademoiselle Lydia. Gratuitous French: He has a French accent and occasionally says French words in his lines. Possibly justified if he was a Frenchman in life.

characters.name: Ginger
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: Beetlejuice calls her "Ginge" from time to time. American Accents: She speaks with a squawky New York accent. The Dead Can Dance: Tap dancing is her biggest passion in (un)life, especially since she has eight legs. The actual quality of her dancing, however, seems to vary by episode. Friendly Neighborhood Spider: Literally. She's one of Beetlejuice's neighbors and is an absolute sweetheart. Unfortunately for her, both qualities make her a frequent target for BJ's pranks. Not So Above It All: She willingly participates in the scheme to humiliate Clare in "Foreign Exchange" as well as the haunted house in "Bizarre Bazaar".

characters.name: The Monster Across the Street
characters.description: Catchphrase: Frequently bellows, "What in tarhooties...?" when he's annoyed by Beetlejuice's shenanigans. Descriptively-Named Species: He's a monster who lives across the street from Beetlejuice. In the episode "It's a Wonderful Afterlife," he instead lives down the block, and his name is changed accordingly. Dreadful Musician: Beetlejuice thinks so, anyway — he really hates the Monster's country-style music. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": He's only ever referred to as "The Monster Across the Street". Expy: He hasGossamer's appearance and Yosemite Sam's mannerisms and verbal tics.

characters.name: Doomie
characters.description: Berserk Button: His "Hyde" side comes out whenever he sees a dog. Cool Car: It's hard to get much cooler than a car which 'talks', drives itself, and flies. Flying Car: Like a lot of things in the Neitherworld, he can hover, although he doesn't do it very often. Happily Adopted: In a way. Some episodes have Beetlejuice and Lydia treating him like he's their son rather than their car. Hopeless Suitor: He falls into this in "Doomie's Romance," when he falls in love with an adorable but non-sentient pink convertible.By the end of the episode, his love for "Pinky" brings her to life.

characters.name: Bea and Nat Juice
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: Bea has a tendency to call everyone "Dear", regardless of whether or not they're a member of her family. The Bore: Their picture is literally in the dictionary under the word "boring." The Dreaded: Beetlejuice is terrified by the idea of Bea visiting him and trying to clean up both him and the Roadhouse. An April Fool's episode had him repeatedly pranking Lydia with his magic. The only time she got him back was when she faked a phone call from Bea saying that she was coming to visit him for a month. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In their debut episode, Bea has dark grey hair and pale greenish skin, but in all following appearances her hair is blonde, her skin is a pale lavender, and she now more closely resembles her two sons. Family Theme Naming: Like their sonBeetlejuice, Bea and Nat are named after insects, specifically bees and gnats.

characters.name: Donny Juice
characters.description: Annoying Younger Sibling: Beetlejuice can't stand how kind, giving, and overly friendly Donny is, to the point that he dreads whenever Donny stops by for a visit. Big Brother Worship: Donny absolutely adores BJ, to the point that he's near oblivious to how much BJ can't stand him. Fall Guy: One of the comic book tie-ins by Harvey Comics, the "Crimebusters on the Haunt" miniseries, has him get in trouble for claiming to be the leader behind the gang of sentient cleaning appliances cleaning up the Neitherworld. It subsequently turns out that he was tricked into taking the fall by the real mastermind. Fluffy Tamer: The "Crimebusters on the Haunt" miniseries establishes that he kept a sandworm namedCuddlesas a pet. Foolish Sibling, Responsible Sibling: Donny is definitely the Responsible Sibling to BJ's Foolish Sibling. In "Midnight Scum", when there's a price on Donny's head for vandalism (he was planting trees all over the Neitherworld, but he was doing it for a benevolent reason), BJ wants to turn him in for the large bounty. Once Donny becomes aware of this, he does the honorable thing and turnshimselfin, and then donates the reward money to charity.

characters.name: Bertha and Prudence
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: In his "Betty Juice" guise, Beetlejuice refers to them as "Burp and Prune." How affectionate the nicknames are is debatable, but he does seem to like both of them. Bespectacled Cutie: Prudence wears round glasses that emphasize her eyes. The Dividual: They're the Syndividual variety, as they aren't remotely identical and have some differing personalities, but don't usually show much indication of individuality and are never seen apart in the show. Goofy Buckteeth: Bertha has these, emphasizing her status as an outcast. Hidden Depths: As revealed in "The Brides of Funkenstein", Prudence has a wild side underneath her mousy exterior, and she admits that she's always wanted to become a rockstar.

characters.name: Clare Brewster
characters.description: '60s Hair: She wears her hair in a large bouffant with two flips. Alpha Bitch: She's the standard popular girl at school who's mean as heck. Certain episodes show she's not even as popular as she thinks she is. No one voted for her for class president (the only vote she got was from herself), everyone hated her haunted house at the school carnival because it wasn't the least bit scary, and her band sucks. Bows for Cuteness: Clare is an ultra-girlyAlpha Bitchwho wears a teal bow in her hair. Bright Is Not Good: To contrast withNice GirlLydia's Gothic fashion, this little brat wears bright pink outfits outside of school. Egocentric Team Naming: Her band is Clare and the Clare-inettes... naturally.

characters.name: Miss Shannon
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: To Beetlejuice's chagrin, she gets a crush on him when he disguises himself as a visiting professor in "Substitute Creature". Adaptational Onscreen Appearance: Her school appeared at the end of the movie, but she makes her first physical appearance in the cartoon. Blah, Blah, Blah: She sometimes lapses into saying "blah" and "drone" during her lessons.

characters.name: Scuzzo the Clown
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: He's the most frequent recurring foe Beetlejuice faces in the series, and their rivalry gets pretty personal. Gag Nose: He has a huge nose. Pungeon Master: Just like his arch-rival Villainous Harlequin: He's a clown and a constant thorn in Beetlejuice's side, though his plans don't usually get any more severe than pranks.

characters.name: Mayor Maynot
characters.description: Berserk Button: He always gets mad at Beetlejuice's pranks, but he getsreally angryat anything that risks his chances at re-election. When he gets publicly slimed and embarrassed in front of the voters, he goes all-out to find Beetlejuice and feed him to the sandworms. Covered in Gunge: Under the influence of Beetlejuice's "New U" cologne, Lydia drenches Mayor Maynot in slime. He mistakenly thinks Beetlejuice did it, and is so angry at the public humiliation that he becomes determined to feed Beetlejuice to the sandworms. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Earlier episodes depicted him as a blue-skinned monster in a top hat and a maroon coat, when the remainder of his appearances made him more of a bandaged invisible man/mummy clad in a blue suit with a red necktie as well as sunglasses. Invisibility: He looks like a mummy, but he's actually an invisible man who covers himself in bandages to be visible to the voters. Mummy: Subverted. He seems like a mummy, but he's actually an invisible man who covers himself in bandages to be visible to the voters. Close-up shots of the Mayor show a gap between the bandages covering his hands and the sleeves of his suit.

characters.name: Mr. Monitor
characters.description: Big Bad: While Scuzzo is the closest thing Beetlejuice has to anArch-Enemy, Mr. Monitor is the closest thing there is to being the main villain of the series. In any interaction between Mr. Monitor and Beetlejuice, the threat of cancellation always hangs over BJ's head and Beetlejuice getting to zap or juice Mr. Monitor is never even presented as a remote possibility. Corrupt Corporate Executive: He'll doanythingfor ratings, including forcing Beetlejuice to continue a dating show he started to get the Monster Across the Street back with his girlfriend and letting aLost in CharacterBeetlejuice hunt an actor playingMoby-Dickfor real. Fat Bastard: He has tremendous girth and is as unscrupulous as they come. Irony: He constantly threatens Beetlejuice with cancellation, yet he debuted in season 4, which as a65-Episode Cartoonwas longer than the first three seasons combined. Karma Houdini Warranty: Most of the time he's able to casually make demands of Beetlejuice or screw around with his life for higher TV ratings. In "The Neitherworld's Least Wanted", all the villains he helped gather together turn on him at the end and beat him up for trying to order them around.

characters.name: Mr. Big
characters.description: Big Bad Wannabe: In "The Neitherworld's Least Wanted", he brings Lipscum, Jesse Germs, Little Miss Warden, and Bartholomew Batt together with a plan to destroy Beetlejuice: get him to say, "I'm coming apart at the seams!", then scatter his body parts and prevent him from reassembling himself before sundown. He appears to be theBig Badwho gathered all of BJ's foes together in aLegion of Doom; but toward the end, he runs away without a fight once Beetlejuice shines a light on him. Mr. Monitor is revealed to beThe Man Behind the Curtainand the trueBig Badof the episode. Mister Big: It's right in his name. He's a powerful mobster who's very short in stature. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Like a lot of cartoon gangsters, his voice is an Edward G. Robinson impression.

characters.name: Lipscum
characters.description: Cephalothorax: He's a giant pair of lips with limbs. The Ditz: He doesn't have much in the "brains" department, even being convinced rather easily by Mr. Monitor that getting a damaged TV set is a better deal than getting his own TV show like the other members of S.N.O.T.R.A.G. Dumbass Has a Point: In spite of being the least intelligent of the assembled villains in "The Neitherworld's Least Wanted", he's the first one to correctly deduce Mr. Big's plan. The Friend Nobody Likes: He's so obnoxious that evenBeetlejuicecan't stand him and he gets on the nerves of BJ's other enemies in "The Neitherworld's Least Wanted" to the degree that they all give him aBig "SHUT UP!" Not-So-Harmless Villain: While generally regarded as a joke, he's the only member of S.N.O.T.R.A.G. in "The Neitherworld's Least Wanted" to succeed in tricking Beetlejuice into saying, "I'm coming apart at the seams!"

characters.name: Jesse Germs
characters.description: Dem Bones: He's a living skeleton. No Celebrities Were Harmed: His voice is an imitation ofClint Eastwood. No Historical Figures Were Harmed: His character is based on the real-lifeOutlawJesse James, with his name even being aa pun on it. Outlaw: He's a skeleton cowboy-outlaw based on real-life outlawJesse James. Professional Killer: Hires himself out to those needing someone to "eliminate" their adversaries.

characters.name: Bartholomew Batt
characters.description: Alliterative Name: Both his first and last name start with the letter B. Card-Carrying Villain: By his own admission, he does what he does because he's a typical cartoon bad guy. Corrupted Character Copy: He's a parody of Mickey Mouse, as one can tell by his being an anthropomorphic cartoon character based on a small mammal with anAlliterative Name, even running a theme park called "Grislyland". However, while Mickey is generally mischievous at worst, Bartholomew is aself-proclaimed"typical cartoon bad guy". Diminishing Villain Threat: His power is easily on par with Beetlejuice's in his first appearance, with their battle leaving Beetlejuice battered and injured, while Bartholomew was able to heal up easily once he got the news he wanted and walk it off like nothing happened to him. By his second appearance, however, Bartholomew is much more easily taken out by Beetlejuice, with or without backup from other villains. Mocky Mouse: He has several overt similarities to Mickey Mouse, with the most notable Mickey-influenced attributes being that his name is an alliteration, he's an anthropomorphic cartoon character based on a small mammal and he runs a theme park called Grislyland (an obvious play on Disneyland).

characters.name: Little Miss Warden
characters.description: Adorable Evil Minions: Several teddy bears work for her, complete with police uniforms andLawman Batons. She also has apartnernamedBilly Club. Enfant Terrible: A little girl who's in charge of a jail system that brainwashes prisoners into being cute and cuddly. Hat of Authority: Her pointed blue hat, which has a badge with aWicked Heart Symbol. Nothing Nice About Sugar and Spice: She likes frilly dresses, has long blonde ringlets, and brainwashes her prisoners into cute, cuddly versions of their former selves. Sinister Shades: Never seen without her dark glasses.

characters.name: Prince Vince
characters.description: Dreadful Musician: In his second appearance he becomes a rock star, but the song he writes depresses everyone who hears it and his singing is terrible. Even so, no one in the Neitherworld can bring themselves to tell him the truth. The Eeyore: Vince is constantly gloomy and, much like theTrope Namer, is often accompanied by literal rain clouds. Expy: Of the titular character fromTim Burton's 1982 stop-motion shortVincent- in name, looks, and even their overdramatic personalities. Fisher King: If Vince is in a particularly sad mood, rain will fall in the area surrounding him, much to the general annoyance of members of his court. Hopeless Suitor: He falls in love with Lydia and asks her to be his princess but sheonly wants to be friends.

characters.name: BarryMeNot
characters.description: Art Shift: Aside from the obvious, he is depicted in 2D during the original intro. In the second intro, he is CGI like in the show itself. Large-Ham Announcer: He tends to emphasize practically every other word when promoting products. Medium Blending: While the cartoon is traditionally animated, his commercials utilized someveryprimitive use of CGI for the time the show was made. The show predatesToy Storyby several years, which should give an idea of how the CGI looked at the time. Punny Name: His name is a pun on the phrase "bury me not", from thefamous cowboy folk song "Bury Me Not on the Lone Prairie".

characters.name: Sandworms
characters.description: Deader than Dead: Given that being fed to the sandworms is one of the worst punishments you can suffer in the Neitherworld, it's implied that any ghost eaten by a sandworm is permanently destroyed as if they'd been exorcised. No wonder Beetlejuice is so scared of them. The Dreaded: The Apex predator of the Neitherworld, and one of the few beings Beetlejuice truly fears. Being eaten by one is implied to permanently destroy you, whether you're a living human or a ghost like Beetlejuice. More Teeth than the Osmond Family: Their mouths are filled with fangs. Purple Is Powerful: In the cartoon, their stripes are two shades of purple rather than black and white. They're also some of the most powerful creatures in the Neitherworld. Roar Before Beating: Sandworms scream in rage as they attack their prey.

characters.name: Beetlejuice (Theatre)
characters.description: The titular character and the Ghost with the Most. Adaptational Angst Upgrade: He's a lot more openly upset aboutthe restrictions he faces in deaththan any other official version of the character. Adaptational Attractiveness: The musical tones down Beetlejuice's rot, removes his greasy hair and gives him a younger, healthier appearance. Notably he's at his grungiest at the very start of the show, in the graveyard, and his cleanest during the wedding scene (where even his wild hair is tamed, intentionally by the other characters), while in his final scene it's hidden by a hat. Adaptational Nice Guy: In the movie, Betelgeuse very clearly had the hots for an underage Lydia and was openly perverted in his behavior towards her. This take on him, however, shows absolutely no indication of lusting after her and she's notably one of the few characters hedoesn'thit on; he still plans to marry her, but he also makes it very clear that it's just something akin to aCitizenship Marriageand he has absolutely no intentions of actually consummating it. Adaptational Villainy:While not wholly or irredeemably evil, he's still depicted in a much darker light than his original counterpart from the movie (though most of it isPlayed for Laughs), and definitelymuchdarker than the cartoon:This version of Betelgeuse manipulates the Maitlands from the start instead of merely being hired by them and then going into his schemes. He plans pretty much everything that happens to them.He's way, way more into killing people, much to the horror of whoever is listening to him at the time.In the movie, Beetlejuice has a moment of empathy when Lydia confesses she's suicidal, and goes as far as to offer to talk to her if she frees him. In this version, he doesn't try to save Lydia from her suicide out of the kindness of his heart, but rather to manipulate her into saying his name three times.Subverted with the wedding and his relationship with Lydia. Beetlejuice is overall much more lecherous towards Lyd

characters.name: The Maitlands
characters.description: A loving couple, Barbara and Adam Maitland perish in a gruesome accident and return to their home as ghosts. Adaptational Dye-Job: Barbara is a brunette in the film, but is played by the blonde Kerry Butler in the original cast. Adaptational Wimp: The Maitlands are depicted as a squeaky clean and overly-polite suburban couple here, and are much worse at scaring people than their movie counterparts (they were able to pull off some genuinely terrifying scares in the film, they just couldn't be seen). Adaptational Sexuality: This version of Adam is either bisexual or very good at faking it. Adaptation Personality Change: Adam and Barbara in the original film were essentially sweet, normal people intended as audience surrogates, and while Adam was a little bit of aCloud Cuckoolanderthey were both very grounded, as well as pretty good at coming up with scares, just not at being seen performing them. Here they're essentially Brad and Janet if they never made it to Frank's castle, and too set in their milquetoast ways to have basically any idea of how to scare anyone until Lydia collaborates with them.

characters.name: Delia
characters.description: Lydia's life coach, who is secretly having an affair with Charles. Adaptational Dumbass: While slightly ditzy and off-beat in the original movie, she is depicted in this version as an airhead who adheres to pseudoscientific New Age woo. Adaptational Nice Guy: Movie!Delia was apathetic to her stepdaughter for most of the movie, not showing any sign of care for her until Betelgeuse arrives. It's implied this sour relationship is one reason for Lydia's depression. In this version, Delia is nice to Lydia from the start and generally wants to help her, but she can't get on Lydia's wavelength. Adaptation Name Change: This version mentions her maiden name is "Schlimmer," as she doesn't become a Deetz until after the events of the musical. The Dog Bites Back: She allows Betelgeuse to torture Otho after he confesses he's a fraud who took advantage of her depression.

characters.name: Maxie and Maxine Dean
characters.description: Associates of Charles Deetz and a wealthy real estate couple. Adaptational Nice Guy: While they still aren't saints, the Deans in this version are slightly better than their movie counterparts. They are friendly old chums to the Deetzes, and although they are somewhat loud and obnoxious, they are still polite to Lydia, Maxie complimenting her when she arrives. It's a step-up from movie-Maxie shushing Lydia during the séance anddisregarding what she says, and calling Charles a putz after a call. Adaptation Name Change: Sarah Dean is renamed Maxine in this version. Adaptation Personality Change: In the movie, the Deans are cold, unfeeling jerks. In this version, they are a boorish, hedonistic couple, with Maxie beingBig Funand Maxine being aBrainless Beauty. Big Fun: Maxie is an overweight, middle-aged man, but he seems like a joy to be around.

characters.name: Emily Deetz
characters.description: Adaptation Expansion: Emily is never mentioned in the movie, and it's never explained how Delia became Lydia's stepmother. In this version, she got very sick and died, although she accepted her fate by the time it happened. Adaptation Name Change: According toan early draft of the script for the movie, her name was originally Evelyn. Death by Adaptation: Retroactively;Beetlejuice Beetlejuicereveals that Lydia's birth mother is actually alive but estranged from the family in the films' continuity. The Ghost: Pun not intended. As Emily is dead, she is reminisced about by the characters, especially Lydia and Charles. Even when Lydia goes to the Neitherworld in an attempt to find her, she still can't, as the Neitherworld is too big and empty. The Lost Lenore: She functions as a non-romantic one to her daughter, who misses her dearly and will do whatever to have her back. Downplayed with her husband, as while he misses her, too, he accepts she's not coming back and is trying to make himself and Lydia happy by being with Delia.

characters.name: Beetlejuice Clones
characters.description: Blue-and-Orange Morality: They share their creator's kooky, perverted nature. Strangely, however, they do haveslightly higher standardsthan him (see below). Everybody Has Standards: After Beetlejuice decides to get the teenage Lydia to marry him so he can become human, the clones are noticeably disgusted, at least until Beetlejuice explains he means a"green card thing"and "strictly business." Evil Minions: They serve as this to Beetlejuice and follow him into the Neitherworldafter he's killed by Lydia. Self-Duplication: They are all clones of Beetlejuice and share hisBlue-and-Orange Morality. Summon Backup Dancers: Beetlejuice brings them to life during "That Beautiful Sound" to help him and Lydia scare people who wander by the house.

characters.name: Sky
characters.description: Bring My Brown Pants: She soils herself after Beetlejuice and Lydia scare her. Canon Foreigner: She is a new character created specifically for the musical. Delicate and Sickly: As Sky mentions in her song, she was born with heart arrhythmia and "could be killed by a random sneeze," but the Girl Scouts helped her deal with this. Still, she wasn't allowed to sell cookies until she's a teen around Lydia's age. Her heart condition almost kills her when Lydia and Beetlejuice scare her, but she manages to run away in fright.In the DC tryout, she survives Beetlejuice scaring her, but is chased away by his clones and has her cookies stolen. In the DC tryout, she survives Beetlejuice scaring her, but is chased away by his clones and has her cookies stolen. Too Dumb to Live: Is very naïve and sheltered, ringing the bell to the Deetz house that has been enchanted by Beetlejuice's magic and agrees to enter Lydia's house because "nobody gets molested by a Goth-y teen."
